correctness.rationale: The Fraïssé age has free amalgamation because T3 is complete. Each unary type is an admissible ternary sign vector; a directed pair is a compatible ordered pair of such vectors; the no-arc channel is the Cartesian square. Thus \(t_1=q\) and \(t_2=q^2+2R\). The C++17 exhaustive program checks every \(3^{\binom{n}{2}}\) labelled assignment for \(0\le n\le5\), every possible forbidden triple, each unary vector and pair compatibility, and all \(n!\) permutations and global reversal; it returns labelled class counts 1,1,3,21,317,9735, quotient class counts 1,1,2,5,17,79, and exactly one double signature fiber at n=5, represented by codes 3048 and 3124 with \((q,R)=(44,973)\). Their underlying graphs differ by presence of a triangle. The t3 identity counts the 0-, 1-, 2- and cyclic-3-arc diagrams, and the corresponding exact integer matrices yield \(t_3(G_A)=653452\) and \(t_3(G_B)=658282\). Independently written Python code checks all admissible 3-new-vertex diagram assignments and reproduces both numbers. Checks are exact; the exhaustive assertion is intentionally finite.

value.rationale: The scalar extension-orbit profile of a named finite base is a natural invariant for oligomorphic homogeneous structures. Its exact reconstruction cutoff and first nonconverse failure are structural rather than arbitrary numeric slices. Exhaustively identifying the unique first collision after quotienting the automatic global-converse symmetry, and proving a third-arity gap of 4830, explains the information lost at low arities. The object and cutoff are motivated independently of the specific integer witnesses; all classification cases are covered, and finite exhaustive computation is appropriate to this exact natural threshold.
